ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
To rescue a patient, an ambulance urgently departs, sounding its siren, and begins to move with uniform acceleration along a horizontal straight road from rest at $t=0$, with an acceleration magnitude of $a=2\mathsf{m}/\mathsf{s}^{2}$. At $t_{1}=10s$, it ceases acceleration and begins to move with uniform velocity. At some later time, the ambulance stops sounding its siren. The last sound of the siren is heard by a person at the ambulance's starting point at $t_{2}=41s$. The speed of sound is given as $v_{0}=340m/s$.

1. What is the magnitude of the ambulance's velocity during its uniform motion?
2. What is the distance of the ambulance from its starting point at the moment it stops sounding its siren?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: To rescue a patient, an ambulance urgently departs, sounding its siren, and begins to move with uniform acceleration along a horizontal straight road from rest at t = 0, with an acceleration magnitude of a = 2 m/s^2. At t1 = 10 s, it ceases acceleration and begins to move with uniform velocity. At some later time, the ambulance stops sounding its siren. The last sound of the siren is heard by a person at the ambulance's starting point at t2 = 41 s. The speed of sound is v0 = 340 m/s. 1. What is the magnitude of the ambulance's velocity during its uniform motion? 2. What is the distance of the ambulance from its starting point at the moment it stops sounding its siren?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Let τ be the absolute time when the ambulance stops sounding its siren. During the first 10 s it starts from rest and accelerates uniformly with a = 2 m/s^2, so the speed at t1 is v = a t1 = 2 × 10 = 20 m/s. The distance covered during this acceleration phase is x1 = (1/2) a t1^2 = (1/2) × 2 × 10^2 = 100 m. Since the siren stops after t1, the ambulance is then moving uniformly at 20 m/s. Its position at time τ is x(τ) = x1 + v(τ - t1) = 100 + 20(τ - 10) = 20τ - 100. The last sound is emitted at time τ from distance x(τ) from the starting point, and it is heard at the starting point at t2 = 41 s. Therefore its travel time is 41 - τ, and its travel distance is 340(41 - τ). Set this equal to the emission distance: 340(41 - τ) = 20τ - 100. Solving: 13940 - 340τ = 20τ - 100, so 14040 = 360τ, hence τ = 39 s. Then x(τ) = 20 × 39 - 100 = 680 m.
